record.final_answer:
Found one fact on the shelf:

Saltmarsh CI hosted runners (docs.saltmarsh.example/limits, read 2026-08-21): a job is cancelled after 6 hours; a whole pipeline run after 72 hours; jobs queued more than 24 hours are dropped; self-hosted runners have no job time limit.

So a 7-hour nightly job on hosted runners gets killed at the 6-hour mark — the 72-hour pipeline limit doesn't rescue it, since the per-job cancellation bites first. Your options: run it on a self-hosted runner, or split the work across jobs that each finish under 6 hours (relying on the 72-hour run limit). Also watch the 24-hour queue cap if runner availability is tight — a nightly job stuck in queue for a day is silently dropped.

Caveat: that's a vendor doc read two months ago; if you're betting a nightly pipeline on it, re-read that limits page before committing.
